content: The title of #40157 should be in my opinion "chore(RingTheory/ClassGroup): deprecate module", but the script that checks the title complains since it thinks RingTheory/ClassGroup is a module. The point is that RingTheory/ClassGroup is both a module and a directory (it has been split, this is why RingTheory/ClassGroup is gone). I think this situation is pretty standard, do we want to fix the script? cc @Michael Rothgang and @Bryan Gin-ge Chen
I think the script should not block merging, it just leaves a comment which you can hide / delete if you want.

Riccardo Brasca said:

The title of #40157 should be in my opinion "chore(RingTheory/ClassGroup): deprecate module", but the script that checks the title complains since it thinks RingTheory/ClassGroup is a module.

The run you sent ran on the title chore(RingTheory.ClassGroup): deprecate module, if you use the title you suggested above I think the linter would be fine with it.
You're right, I didn't think about the difference between / and ., thanks!
So everything already works, sorry for the noise.
Maybe we should fix the error message to explain the issue better? e.g. suffix it with (the scope contains a dot, use forward slashes instead)
I've seen this thread and will try to make a PR fixing this tomorrow!
#40177 improves the error message. I wordsmithed the wording a bit.

In #40335 I got this warning because of 1000.yaml :sweat_smile:
We should add exceptions for the extensions ["bib", "json", "md", "py", "sh", "toml", "txt", "yaml", "yml"].
We could exempt anything that .endsWith these extensions, but perhaps we want to allow doc(1000.yaml,Archive): ..., so I'm thinking scope.replace ("." + extension) "" for all the extensions before checking .contains '.'.
Wdyt?
